feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Jazz legend John Coltrane's Philadelphia house to become a cultural heritage site
entry.summary: On the centennial of father's birth, Ravi Coltrane talks about turning the home where the jazz legend spent a crucial period in the 1950s into a cultural heritage and community space.

entry.title: U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for missile attacks on Navy ships
entry.summary: One of the Iranian tankers struck was near a key area in Iran's oil-export system, according to U.S. Central Command.

entry.title: Opinion: A sculpture in perpetual motion, removed
entry.summary: "Blue," a statue that's been on the grounds of the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C. for 7 years has been dismantled and removed.

entry.title: Trump administration to dig at triumphal arch site despite no final federal approvals
entry.summary: The Trump administration says it will break ground on a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., without final federal approval and despite an ongoing lawsuit.

entry.title: U.S.-Venezuela oil deal puts opposition in a political bind
entry.summary: Venezuelan opposition members are uneasy with new oil deals with the U.S., worried that agreements with authoritarian regime in Caracas could undermine democratic progress.

entry.title: Whatever happened to the floating schools of Bangladesh?
entry.summary: It was a light bulb moment: If monsoon rains keep kids from safely getting to school, let's create a floating school to pick them up! Bangladesh pioneered the idea. How's it doing?

entry.title: U.S. envoys in Moscow in new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
entry.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to revive efforts to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a halt to air attacks during their visit, but Moscow has not publicly responded.

entry.title: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are trying to cash in for midterms
entry.summary: Democrats and Republicans have found common ground in this campaign season. Both parties have poured millions into ads attacking data centers as the public continues to protest the AI facilities.

entry.title: Flock cameras draw opposition from across the political spectrum
entry.summary: As political races heat up heading into the midterms, candidates from both parties are increasingly joining the fray to voice concerns over Flock surveillance cameras.

entry.title: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posts bail after arrest
entry.summary: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte has posted bail after order issued for her arrest on charges she publicly threatened to arrange assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two others.
